technology use has positive effect of student engagement and self directed behavior which in turn has positive effect of academic performance.
the technology usage is positively associated with self directed learning and student engagement, and indirectly with the academic performance.
the students' technology usage has positive effects on their engagement and self directed behaviors, which in turn affect their academic performance.

the interrelations of the technology with student engagement, academic performance and self directed learning.
the impact of technology on academic performance, self directed learning (SDl), and engagement of students in higher education.
the relationship of technology with academic performance and other related constructs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
technology use has positive effect in the academic performance through the mediating role of self directed learning.
the students' technology usage has positive effect on their academic performance through self directed learning and student engagement.
the use of technology has positive effects on student engagement and self directed leaning, and both these academic behaviors in turn affect the academic performance of the students.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
technology use has a positive effect on self-directed learning, student engagement, but no direct effect on academic performance.
the students' technology usage has a positive effect on their engagement and self directed leaning, which in turn affect their academic performance.
students' technology use is positively associated with self directed learning, which in turn has a significant positive relationship with academic performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
technology use has a direct positive impact on self directed learning and student engagement but not on the academic performance.
the relationship between technology use and student engagement is not direct, but mediated by self directed learning.
technology is not an independent factor that affects student learning and academic performance, rather it is the way students use technology that determines the impact.
